title: SDLC
objectives: List the phases of the software development lifecycle
Explain where testing and CI/CD fit

sections.markdown: The Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) is the structured process teams use to plan, build, test, deploy and maintain software.

sections.code:
Requirements -> Design -> Implementation -> Testing
   -> Deployment -> Maintenance  (and loop back)

sections.markdown: Waterfall is building a house from a fixed blueprint; Agile is sculpting — you shape, get feedback, and adjust each iteration.
Shift testing left (write tests early), automate with CI/CD, and ship small increments. Small, frequent releases are safer than big-bang launches.

flashcards.back: Requirements, Design, Implementation, Testing, Deployment, Maintenance.
Waterfall = sequential, fixed plan. Agile = iterative sprints adapting to change.
Testing early in the lifecycle to catch defects when they're cheap to fix.

quiz.q: Which model suits rapidly changing requirements?
quiz.explain: Agile's short iterations absorb change better than sequential Waterfall.
Continuous Integration/Delivery automates building, testing and shipping.
Catch defects early when they're cheapest to fix.
